clue.text: Heads of business events arrive in suit

indicators.note: the heads of words are their leading letters, so only the opening letter of each is kept

parts.note: the first letters of these two words
to arrive is to come

explanation.surface: Office managers turn up at corporate functions dressed in their suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like a noun about clothing, but it is the verb, as in 'that colour suits you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To become someone is to look good on them or be fitting for them, the same verbal sense as suit.

clue.text: Large adult gets possessive, having multiple partners

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for a noun; read as 'the state of having multiple partners'

parts.note: large means big
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
my is a possessive word

explanation.surface: A big grown-up turns jealous and clingy, all while juggling several lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is the offence of being married to two spouses at once, a case of multiple partners.

clue.text: Company representative: legit or involved in crime?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a Member of Parliament is an elected representative
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a firm's agent is above board or a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Being complicit means sharing guilt as an accomplice in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Tuneful Sporty Spice keeping marriage vow up

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Sporty Spice of the Spice Girls is Mel C

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: the vow said at a wedding

explanation.surface: A pop singer keeps her wedding promise in a melodious way.
explanation.walkthrough: Sporty Spice, Melanie Chisholm of the 1990s Spice Girls, is known as Mel C; her name splits around the reversed vow.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic describes music with a pleasing tune, so it is a synonym of tuneful.

clue.text: Enchantress, in coat of suede and diamonds, getting changed

indicators.note: placed in means sitting inside the other letters
a coat is the outside layer, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of suede
an enchantress is a witch
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A sorceress in a suede jacket and diamond jewellery is having a costume change.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched means swapped or altered, a synonym of changed.

clue.text: Harry and William's undomesticated beasts

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The two princes, Harry and William, own some untamed creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' reads as Prince Harry beside his brother, but it is a verb meaning harass, signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild animals are creatures living untamed, not kept as pets or livestock.

clue.text: Peculiar haste over work in cafe

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone works in a cafe with an odd kind of hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' just puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea shop is a small British restaurant serving tea and light meals, much like a cafe.

clue.text: Boring house husband? I'm not sure

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
H is the abbreviation for husband
um is the noise of hesitation

explanation.surface: Is a stay-at-home husband dull? The speaker isn't convinced.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum is an adjective for something dull and unexciting, the same as boring.

clue.text: Ruins of French ship around city of Paris

parts.note: de is the French for of

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
Paris of Greek legend was a prince of Troy

explanation.surface: Remains of a French vessel lie somewhere around the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city of Paris' suggests the French capital, but this Paris is the Trojan prince whose city was Troy. 'Ruins' is a verb, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to wreck it completely, so destroys is a synonym of ruins as a verb.

clue.text: Wager ultimately losing? Proceed at a slow pace

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of losing
to amble is to walk slowly

explanation.surface: A punter, sure to lose in the end, trudges along slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamble is a bet placed on an uncertain outcome, the same as a wager.

clue.text: Drains colour from sandy areas around lake

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps the single letter

parts.note: beaches are sandy stretches of shore
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Pale sand around a lake seems to wash the colour out of the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleach is a whitening agent, and to bleach something is to remove its colour.

clue.text: Role madam plays in sensational story

indicators.note: to play is to fool around with something, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: An actress takes the part of a brothel-keeper in a lurid drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a story with exaggerated, sensational events and emotions.

clue.text: Writer is entertaining match officials

parts.note: a writer is an author

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a tie is a sporting match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A novelist is hosting the referees from a football game.
explanation.definitionFit: The authorities are the people in charge, the officials who hold power.

clue.text: Filled with love, His Majesty King Edward is Mrs Simpson's husband

indicators.note: something filled with an item holds it inside, so the letters are packed into another piece

parts.note: HM is the abbreviation for His Majesty
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: Edward VIII, besotted, is the husband of Wallis Simpson.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Wallis Simpson, for whom Edward VIII abdicated; the Mrs Simpson meant is Marge of the cartoon The Simpsons.
explanation.definitionFit: In the TV cartoon The Simpsons, Marge's husband is Homer, so he is Mrs Simpson's husband.

clue.text: Might you find old-fashioned drinkers here?

definitions.text: Might you find old-fashioned drinkers here?

parts.note: surface reading: elderly, traditional people who like a drink, perhaps in a pub
setter's reading: an Old Fashioned is a whisky cocktail, so its drinkers gather at a gathering built around mixed drinks

explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like a description of the drinkers, but it names a classic cocktail made with whisky, sugar and bitters.
explanation.definitionFit: A social gathering where mixed drinks such as an Old Fashioned are served is just where those drinkers would be.

clue.text: Providing cooked dinner consumed by Reginald

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order
what is consumed by someone ends up inside them

parts.note: Reg is the short form of Reginald
the six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a cooked meal that Reginald then eats.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering assistance means giving it, so rendering can stand for providing.

clue.text: The Circle Line? Dear me, it needs renovating!

indicators.note: renovating means doing up and rebuilding, so these letters are remade in a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A passenger groans that the London Underground's Circle Line badly needs repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; read literally it is a line belonging to a circle, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is the straight line through a circle's centre, a line that belongs to the circle.

clue.text: Grilling gratin with roe on it, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals something turning out unexpectedly, so the letters come out in an unforeseen order

parts.note: the letters as written
the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone grills a gratin topped with fish roe, an unexpected combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grilling' sits beside food and looks like cooking, but it means questioning hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to question them intensely, which is what an interrogation is.

clue.text: Rejection of a lot of rubbish by a student

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: refuse is household waste
taken as written
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A student's pile of junk gets turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: A learner is a student, and L is the letter on a British learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a saying no, the same as a rejection.

clue.text: Maybe flies home with the Amish and the Quakers?

parts.note: being in means being at home
both are religious groups, or sects

explanation.surface: Does someone travel by air back to a community of Amish and Quakers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun, an example of the answer, as 'Maybe' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Flies are one example of small six-legged creatures, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: European leaves e.g. Donatello's works standing

indicators.note: what leaves departs, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: Donatello was a Renaissance sculptor whose works are statues
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European walks away from the Renaissance sculptures still on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' could be foliage and 'standing' a statue's pose, but they are the deletion signal and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is rank or position in society, which is what one's standing means.

clue.text: Pattern of female and one male cat from the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
the Roman numeral for one
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A design shows a she-cat and a tomcat from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a repeated design element, a pattern in decoration.

clue.text: Yes-man's publicity plugging plaything

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a toy is a plaything
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A sycophant's marketing campaign is plugging a toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' looks like promoting a product, but it means filling a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a fawning flatterer who agrees with the boss, just like a yes-man.

clue.text: Determined sibling enters where campers are

indicators.note: what enters something goes inside it

parts.note: campers sleep in a tent
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A stubborn sister pushes her way into the campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insistent means firmly refusing to give way, so it means determined.

clue.text: Pass on motorway during journey

indicators.note: during places something within a span, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: transit is passage from place to place
M is the prefix of British motorway numbers

explanation.surface: A driver overtakes on the motorway in the middle of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' suggests overtaking on the road, but 'Pass on' means hand along. British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to send or convey something to others, the same as pass on.

clue.text: Kind of rock, somewhat kitsch, is tacky

indicators.note: somewhat means to some degree, so only part of the following words is used

parts.note: running across the end of kitsch and into is and tacky

explanation.surface: A style of rock music is called rather tasteless and cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Schist is a metamorphic rock that splits into thin layers.

clue.text: Occasionally groovy celebrities favouring Charles?

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of groovy
the A-list is the top tier of famous people

explanation.surface: Hip celebrities sometimes back a man named Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Charles meant is King Charles III, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist supports the monarchy, so royalist describes someone backing King Charles.

clue.text: Wise person probing American customs

indicators.note: a probe pushes into something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for American
a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: A wise scholar investigates the traditions of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages are habitual practices or conventions, which is what customs are.
